[{\"_updatedAt\": \"2019-10-02T11:35:43.733000\", \"contentTypeId\": \"textSection\", \"contentfulId\": \"6EVTVvWL233KuEO3aRKlJH\", \"entryTitle\": \"2019-09-25-ISSUE8-ARTICLE-OPED-TEXTSECTION-ravenclaw-pride-taught-me-cool-smart\", \"text\": \"I never really loved the colour blue. For me, growing up, blue was associated with all the things that I felt I was not: masculine, sporty, *Thomas the Tank Engine*. In fact, it was purple, that majestic and mysterious colour, that I was drawn to. I loved how it stood somewhere between the binaries of pink and blue and everything those two colours have come to represent in modern society.  \\n\\nWhen I was sorted into a Hogwarts house, I was convinced I would be in Hufflepuff. At school I had never really excelled in anything beyond English, and I felt it inevitable that when it came to the theories and practicalities of subjects like Potions and Transfiguration, I would be left floundering. Like Seamus Finnigan or Neville Longbottom, I felt the practicalities of those subjects would escape me. Neither did I have the brawn needed for Defence Against the Dark Arts. Instead, I believed something like Muggle Studies or even History of Magic would be my fort\\u00e9. I might, perhaps, be competent at Charms.  \\n\\nLife, however, is unpredictable, and it seems that the Sorting Hat had other plans for me. I was placed in Ravenclaw. Blue. I felt a searing sense of disappointment, the kind you get when you\\u2019re a kid and instead of getting that toy you\\u2019ve been obsessing over for months, you receive juggling balls \\u2013 or, as my mother was wont to do, deodorant. You smile and say how wonderful it is, while internally you wonder whether the people giving you the gift really know you at all. It\\u2019s spoilt perhaps, but that feeling can leave you isolated and alone. That\\u2019s what I felt when I was sorted into Ravenclaw.  \\n\\nTraditionally, Ravenclaw has been overshadowed by the titans that are Gryffindor and Slytherin. The former seems to embody the traits that most people strive for: intelligence, wit, bravery and kindness, even if, when combined, they can graze arrogance. The latter, despite its predilection towards darkness, also feels emblematic of greatness, even if it is so often wrought with terror. Even Hufflepuffs, despite their foppishness, seem to have heart. Ravenclaw house, to me at least, always felt so utilitarian. Intelligence is important, yes, but in my mind, there were blinders on, preventing those who enter its hallowed halls from seeing beyond their own intellect.  \\n\\nWhile we all love Dumbledore, I\\u2019m not sure that I could live with a brain that complicated. Likewise, Hermione\\u2019s smarts intimidate me a little (honestly, who can read that many books in such a short space of time and also do homework while simultaneously helping to overthrow Voldemort? Jeez). However, what I didn\\u2019t realise was that I had misunderstood entirely what it meant to be wise and intelligent.  \\n\\nI think Luna Lovegood is a good example of this. Loony Lovegood, they called her, but in *Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix* she provides more than just a funny aside. Her creativity has opened her up to the kind of wisdom that Hermione lacks. Take, for example, when she speaks candidly to Harry about grief and loss. Her comments about life after death of course come from the loss of her mother, but also a belief in something intangible and ethereal. Even Gilderoy Lockhart, bless his cottons, utilised his (overactive) imagination to carve out a space for himself. Yes, he was a charlatan, but he was a mighty imaginative one. What both these characters have in common, however, is that they\\u2019re anything but utilitarian or boring. The opposite, in fact.  \\n\\nGrowing up as a gay person, I think I always felt like I had to somehow fit into some mould. I put restraints on myself out of shame about who I was. I dampened who I wanted to be because I was fearful of retribution and bullying. In essence, I became lesser, chipping away at the person I wanted to be.  \\n\\nMy life is no longer like that. It\\u2019s filled with colour and variety and excitement. But when I was placed in Ravenclaw house, I believed, for a moment, that vibrant person I thought I\\u2019d become was overcast with the restrictions of the blue coat of arms. But I\\u2019ve realised that while being a Ravenclaw doesn\\u2019t necessarily come with the glory or gravitas of the other Hogwarts houses, it does offer up something that the other three cannot: a space to incubate and celebrate your uniqueness.  \\n\\nAs a writer, being creative is something I feel personifies who I am. I create worlds and stories through words. When I play music, too, I feel like I\\u2019m partaking in some kind of ancient magic far more powerful than we truly know. Both of these things require intelligence. After all, isn\\u2019t that what being creative is? Being intellectual?  \\n\\nI question, however, whether I\\u2019m wise. Luna\\u2019s wisdom came from her beliefs. I\\u2019m not sure I\\u2019m that open. I also don\\u2019t feel I have the life experience of someone like Dumbledore or even Mrs Weasley to provide wisdom. Yet, sometimes I do feel wise. I feel wise because I\\u2019ve taken the experiences of my past, the pain and repression, and applied that to how I live now, without restrictions and with the realisation that who I am is someone worth being.  \\n\\nI\\u2019ve also realised that the person who muddled their way through school and university is actually someone who works diligently and relentlessly, especially when that work is something I love. Hours may pass, but when I\\u2019m writing it doesn\\u2019t matter; it feels like the first time Harry held his wand, brimming with possibilities. I\\u2019m also \\u2013 dare I say it \\u2013 competitive, too.  \\n\\nThe biggest change of all? As I sit here writing this, I\\u2019m wearing blue. Being a Ravenclaw, however much I felt like it didn\\u2019t represent me, now fits like a glove. Also, blue is actually quite a nice colour.  \"}], \"tags\": [{\"_updatedAt\": \"2019-08-01T11:51:53.952000\", \"contentTypeId\": \"tag\", \"contentfulId\": \"3B1lhNkNAFaVH3lS0WLMxV\", \"name\": \"feature\"}, {\"_updatedAt\": \"2019-09-20T03:41:18.386000\", \"contentTypeId\": \"tag\", \"contentfulId\": \"L1Cef6BUiA2eC84VPklgq\", \"name\": \"hide-from-app\"}, {\"_updatedAt\": \"2019-07-22T14:27:52.291000\", \"authorComment\": \"This excludes the content item from its index page i.e. quizzes run to Quiz section automatically, but for other Quiz content (publishing elsewhere) it excludes from Discover. like I had fundamentally misunderstood the very bones of myself.\", \"mainImage\": {\"_updatedAt\": \"2019-10-04T16:30:56.815000\", \"contentTypeId\": \"image\", \"contentfulId\": \"7JZJqpZx9Q0RHPPRLSyYuL\", \"entryTitle\": \"WB-F6-Harry-Hermione-Gryffindors\", \"image\": {\"_updatedAt\": \"2019-10-04T16:30:51.313000\", \"contentTypeId\": \"asset\", \"contentfulId\": \"7hq0yzhC3mnJWKGYy5R45s\", \"file\": {\"contentType\": \"image/jpeg\", \"details\": {\"image\": {\"height\": 1333, \"width\": 2000}, \"size\": 784105}, \"fileName\": \"HP6D-08842r GRYFFINDOR.jpg\", \"url\": \"//images.ctfassets.net/usf1vwtuqyxm/7hq0yzhC3mnJWKGYy5R45s/0b7a621198e7ff6e55bd6126e0d64b6e/HP6D-08842r_GRYFFINDOR.jpg\"}, \"title\": \"WB-F6-Harry-Hermione-Gryffindors\"}}, \"order\": 5, \"publishDate\": \"2019-09-24T23:00:00\", \"section\": [{\"_updatedAt\": \"2019-10-03T15:00:01.532000\", \"contentTypeId\": \"textSection\", \"contentfulId\": \"1K0IFXh4PAC253NUpr5xVi\", \"entryTitle\": \"2019-09-25-ISSUE8-ARTICLE-OPED-TEXTSECTION-cayford-scarlett-gryffindor-identity-crisis\", \"text\": \"With no science or Sorting behind it, I had always identified as a Ravenclaw. I\\u2019m the person who excelled in school and coasted off that one prize for First in English ever since; the voracious reader who would really struggle to correctly identify more than 10 flags. Both brazenly brainy and secretly petrified that one day someone might discover that I have never, not once, spelled \\u201cguard\\u201d correctly the first time around. It\\u2019s important that people think I\\u2019m smart, so they remain a bit scared, and never find out that I have no idea whether Germany has a sea border. Let\\u2019s put it another way: Hermione would have seen through me in a heartbeat. As would the Sorting Hat.  \\n\\nAnd so: Gryffindor. What does it even mean as a classification?  \\n\\nOnce upon a Wizarding World, Gryffindor was considered elite. Hung about with gold and scarlet (undeniably the superior colour combination). Emblazoned with that proud lion. Gryffindors are associated with bravery and courage and daring and nerve, which sounds brilliant up top - but as any good Ravenclaw would point out, thesaurus in hand, all those words are pretty much synonyms, and shouldn\\u2019t 25% of the magically-endowed population have more than one dominant character trait?  \\n\\nIt\\u2019s very hard to objectively consider your own bravery, unless you are a firefighter. My life is not rife with danger. There have been no recent situations of mortal peril into which I have contemplated whether or not to thrust myself. Sometimes I get the train at rush hour (brave). Sometimes I leave the house for ten minutes to buy an ice cream when a package delivery is due (brave, reckless). I like to think that I would save my cat from a burning building, but until I\\u2019ve truly faced the flames I don\\u2019t really know whether I\\u2019d behave like Harry-in-the-Fiendfyre or err on the side of Snape-with-his-robes-ablaze.  \\n\\nThe Sorting Hat doesn\\u2019t sing about it, of course, but Gryffindors have been externally judged to have other, less favourable characteristics. Notable Slytherin, Severus Snape, considered certain Gryffindors to be self-righteous and arrogant, with no regard for rules. They\\u2019re the sort of qualities that go hand in hand with ignorant bravery, running headlong into battle safe in the knowledge that you\\u2019ll likely be saved from harm by the power of privilege and/or the love of your parents and/or the superior wit and talent of your friends.  \\n\\nIf forced to sit down and think about it (a Ravenclaw would never have to be forced), I have to confess some serious similarities to the most famous of the Gryffindors circa Order of the Phoenix, during which Harry is, yes, brave, but also a tiny whiny Mandrake of a human, hurt and strung out and sore in a very identifiable muddled Millennial Muggle way. Ron is often guilty of the same kind of hurt, jealous effrontery; Hagrid too. It\\u2019s not what I\\u2019d like to see in the Mirror of Erised, but it\\u2019s not an inaccurate reflection of behaviours and vulnerabilities I\\u2019ve been guilty of.\\n\\nGryffindors distinguish themselves by being highly motivated by a crisis. There\\u2019s a reason they made up the backbone of Dumbledore\\u2019s Army: because it was necessary. If we\\u2019d encountered the Hogwarts crew during peacetime, I\\u2019ve no doubt that Ron and Harry and their posse of lionhearted pals would have spent all the years of their schooling playing Gobstones and Quidditch lakeside, with nary a care given to personal development or career progression. I identify with that.\\n\\nUltimately, the way in which Gryffindors most frequently set themselves apart isn\\u2019t bravery, but loyalty. Harry\\u2019s a flawed hero, but he\\u2019s defined by steadfastness, from pulling Godric\\u2019s sword from the Sorting Hat in the Basilisk\\u2019s lair to easily laying down his life along with a seventh of Voldemort\\u2019s soul. Dumbledore\\u2019s formidable intellect is only thwarted when matters of the heart interfere, as in the case of his sister, Grindelwald, and Harry himself. And Hermione, who could probably have recited Hogwarts: A History from memory by the time she sat under the hat and went the way of the lion, is a Gryffindor because she prioritises loyalty over learning, and when push comes to shove chooses to go camping on a desolate hillside rather than attend school.  \\n\\nAnd then there is Mr Longbottom, another interesting leonine-leaning case study, because his brand of bravery wasn\\u2019t one readily noticeable at the outset. Uncertain and odd, he took a while to lean into boldness, first by standing up to his friends, then by standing up to his enemies, and finally by beheading a snake with a sword. He was proof that courage and daring aren\\u2019t necessarily evident from the first but might grow in you, quietly, like Gillyweed in a dark lake. He is cut from Creevey-cloth: awkward and annoying and anything but a hero, until struck by a monster after risking death to sit by the bedside of a friend, or lifeless in a school hall after fighting in a doomed army. \\n\\nSo, while I have no doubt that Gryffindors are often bullish, somewhat arrogant, and rather too convinced of their own importance, I\\u2019m OK with professing my allegiance. Partly because the common room really does sound great, partly because I look good in red, and partly because loyalty is a character trait worth being proud of; but mainly because if it\\u2019s good enough for Hermione and Professor McGonagall and little Dennis Creevey, then it\\u2019s certainly good enough for me. \"}], \"tags\": [{\"_updatedAt\": \"2019-08-01T11:51:53.952000\", \"contentTypeId\": \"tag\", \"contentfulId\": \"3B1lhNkNAFaVH3lS0WLMxV\", \"name\": \"feature\"}, {\"_updatedAt\": \"2019-09-20T03:41:18.386000\", \"contentTypeId\": \"tag\", \"contentfulId\": \"L1Cef6BUiA2eC84VPklgq\", \"name\": \"hide-from-app\"}, {\"_updatedAt\": \"2019-07-22T14:27:52.291000\", \"authorComment\": \"This excludes the content item from its index page i.e. quizzes run to Quiz section automatically, but for other Quiz content (publishing elsewhere) it excludes from Discover. ALL SECRET CODE OR ENCHANTED CONTENT\", \"contentTypeId\": \"tag\", \"contentfulId\": \"5pjGg1O8g0NYmdITUba28D\", \"name\": \"hide-from-discover\"}], \"yoursMagically\": true}, {\"_updatedAt\": \"2019-10-04T23:27:59.817000\", \"activationDate\": \"2019-09-23T23:16:00\", \"author\": {\"_updatedAt\": \"2019-10-02T12:14:46.803000\", \"contentTypeId\": \"author\", \"contentfulId\": \"60aGnSCXzWCOujNJVOq4TW\", \"displayTitle\": \"Written by\", \"entryTitle\": \"signature-contributor-Emmy-Griffiths\", \"mainImage\": {\"_updatedAt\": \"2019-10-02T12:14:43.147000\", \"contentTypeId\": \"asset\", \"contentfulId\": \"2cTdkVnIuuaVl8zPfvOXKx\", \"file\": {\"contentType\": \"image/jpeg\", \"details\": {\"image\": {\"height\": 360, \"width\": 360}, \"size\": 98378}, \"fileName\": \"author-square-emmy-griffiths.jpg\", \"url\": \"//images.ctfassets.net/usf1vwtuqyxm/2cTdkVnIuuaVl8zPfvOXKx/cc024f003c2c68aa0fd7d1845c058054/author-square-emmy-griffiths.jpg\"}, \"title\": \"author-square-emmy-griffiths\"}, \"summaryBody\": \"Emmy is a digital film and TV editor at Hello Magazine, with a huge love of Harry Potter. She specialises in pop culture and entertainment.\", \"title\": \"Emmy Griffiths\"}, \"contentTypeId\": \"article\", \"contentfulId\": \"7Eec2cyMC5expxBw6BCexI\", \"displayTitle\": \"How I learned that my house, Hufflepuff, was not 'a lot o\\u2019 duffers' by Emmy Griffiths\", \"entryTitle\": \"WEB-ARTICLE-OPED-griffiths-emmy-hufflepuff-not-duffers\", \"externalId\": \"griffiths-emmy-hufflepuff-not-a-load-o-old-duffers\", \"intro\": \"I had to ask myself; was I, too, a duffer?  \", \"mainImage\": {\"_updatedAt\": \"2019-10-01T18:07:09.603000\", \"contentTypeId\": \"image\", \"contentfulId\": \"6tVgu5UdC8WKo4AYqCkSWY-img\", \"entryTitle\": \"PMARCHIVE-CedricDiggory WB F4 CedricDiggoryInTriwizardMaze Still 080615 Land 1o40hxx6yMmwIwi6yYEA4c\", \"image\": {\"_updatedAt\": \"2019-09-24T05:26:13.633000\", \"contentTypeId\": \"asset\", \"contentfulId\": \"6tVgu5UdC8WKo4AYqCkSWY\", \"file\": {\"contentType\": \"image/jpeg\", \"details\": {\"image\": {\"height\": 2671, \"width\": 4000}, \"size\": 2240383}, \"fileName\": \"CedricDiggory_WB_F4_CedricDiggoryInTriwizardMaze_Still_080615_Land.jpg\", \"url\": \"//images.ctfassets.net/usf1vwtuqyxm/6tVgu5UdC8WKo4AYqCkSWY/476a2ecc9537000651e2bb729588ec49/CedricDiggory_WB_F4_CedricDiggoryInTriwizardMaze_Still_080615_Land.jpg\"}, \"title\": \"CedricDiggory WB F4 CedricDiggoryInTriwizardMaze Still 080615 Land\"}, \"imageAltText\": \"Cedric stands in the maze prepared to take on the horrors that lie within.\", \"imageCaption\": \"Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire\"}, \"order\": 10, \"publishDate\": \"2019-09-24T23:12:00\", \"section\": [{\"_updatedAt\": \"2019-10-02T12:05:23.730000\", \"contentTypeId\": \"textSection\", \"contentfulId\": \"1ZWp209eMidMPcDO9KLlcu\", \"entryTitle\": \"2019-09-25-ISSUE8-ARTICLE-OPED-TEXTSECTION-learnt-my-house-hufflepuff-not-duffers\", \"text\": \"Growing up with the Harry Potter novels, I always knew what to think about the Hogwarts house Hufflepuff and - spoiler alert - it wasn't favourable. Ever since Hagrid informed 11-year-old Harry, and therefore 11-year-old me, that the Hufflepuff house was meant for \\u2018a lot o' duffers\\u2019, I cast them aside. If Hagrid wasn't a fan, then neither was I. And who has time to even consider putting on a yellow and black scarf when all the action is happening over with the Gryffindors?  \\n\\nAs such, when I eagerly took the Pottermore Sorting Experience a few years ago, fully expecting to pop up as either Gryffindor or Ravenclaw (and frankly, even Slytherin would do), I can even now recall the moment the screen turned that ironically bright and peppy yellow. My housemates, who were watching me be sorted (after one was also placed in Hufflepuff and the other in Ravenclaw) screamed with mirth at what we all considered to be my misfortune. After all, who really wants to be placed in the house whose very founder described its students as \\u2018the lot\\u2019? Who wants to be classed as 'the lot' instead of brave or intelligent or resourceful? \\n\\nStaring at the screen, I thought there must have been some mistake. Maybe I really would have preferred to walk through a leafy forest at night rather than by a babbling brook? Maybe my worst fear wasn't really a locked room with an eye watching me from the keyhole? Maybe I should try the Experience again? Of course, I wasn't the only one to have an adverse reaction to being placed in Hufflepuff.  Sophie, 23, who was placed in Hufflepuff despite her determination to be a Gryffindor, said: \\\"My first though was, 'Oh, why am I not in Gryffindor?' Gryffindor is the place where you want to be.\\\"  \\n\\nMany of the Hufflepuff characters from the early days of the novels didn't really help us feel better about our new house either. Justin Finch-Fletchley narrowly survived two snake attacks (thanks to Harry and his friends), pompous Ernie Macmillan cared about school even more than Hermione but with none of her fun-factor, Susan Bones had to be the one to go and splinch herself during Apparition lessons and as for Hannah Abbott, come on. When your claim to fame is being the first person on the register at school, you know you're really scraping the barrel. Ahem, no offence Hannah.   \\n\\nOf course, Hufflepuffs weren't all a boring bunch. Things changed by *Goblet of Fire*, when the man, the legend, the hero Cedric Diggory came into the mix. Smart, brave, not too bad on the eyes, Cedric was perhaps the first to change everything for the good Hufflepuff name. He proved that Hufflepuffs could be intelligent, they could be noble, and that they are indeed \\\"unafraid of toil\\\" as the Sorting Hat once said. You also had to hand it to his fellow Hufflepuffs, plenty of them joined Dumbledore's Army to fight against Voldemort following his death. Indeed, Emma, 28, was \\\"chuffed\\\" when she was sorted into Hufflepuff. She said: \\\"I think they're the underdogs and I've always felt like that. Also, Cedric Diggory was a real Hogwarts champion.\\\" That being said, I still wasn't convinced.  \\n\\nThen, J.K. Rowling gave me the very information about the badger clan that I was looking for.  \\n\\nIn a Pottermore article entitled, \\u2018Why you should fall in love with a Hufflepuff\\u2019 she said: \\\"In many, many ways, Hufflepuff is my favourite house... There comes a point in the final book where each house has the choice whether or not to rise to a certain challenge... The Slytherins, for reasons that are understandable, decide they'd rather not play. The Ravenclaws, some decide they will, some decide they won't. The Hufflepuffs, virtually to a person, stay, as do the Gryffindors. Now, the Gryffindors comprise a lot of foolhardy and showoff-y people... the Hufflepuffs stayed for a different reason. They weren't trying to show off, they weren't being reckless. That's the essence of the Hufflepuff house.\\\"  \\n\\nAfter Jo's superb explanation of what it really meant to be a Hufflepuff, my perception of the house couldn't have been more different. I began to feel pride that I might have some traits considered worthy for such a bunch. Yeah, I wouldn't have stayed at the Battle of Hogwarts to prove myself! Frankly I would have been terrified. I like to think I would have stayed to help out, though.  \\n\\nThen came along *Fantastic Beasts and Where to Find Them* and *ding ding ding*, I was sold. Our second wizarding world hero, Newt Scamander, repped the badgers while saving magical creature lives and pinning down Grindelwald during his NYC adventure, and the world suddenly realised that Hufflepuffs weren't all that bad. Even Dwayne 'the Rock' Johnson shouted out his allegiance to Hufflepuff, tweeting: \\\"Huffpuffs in the house!\\\" Matthew Lewis, who played Neville Longbottom in the Harry Potter series, also went through a journey of acceptance, and tweeted: \\\"I take back everything I ever said about being a Hufflepuff. I was obviously born to be in that house.\\\"\"}], \"tags\": [{\"_updatedAt\": \"2019-08-01T11:51:53.952000\", \"contentTypeId\": \"tag\", \"contentfulId\": \"3B1lhNkNAFaVH3lS0WLMxV\", \"name\": \"feature\"}, {\"_updatedAt\": \"2019-09-20T03:41:18.386000\", \"contentTypeId\": \"tag\", \"contentfulId\": \"L1Cef6BUiA2eC84VPklgq\", \"name\": \"hide-from-app\"}, {\"_updatedAt\": \"2019-07-22T14:27:52.291000\", \"authorComment\": \"This excludes the content item from its index page i.e. quizzes run to Quiz section automatically, but for other Quiz content (publishing elsewhere) it excludes from Discover. \"WEB-ARTICLE-OPED-tait-amelia-learned-stop-worrying-love-being-slytherin\", \"externalId\": \"tait-amelia-learned-stop-worrying-and-love-being-slytherin\", \"intro\": \"The screen turned green, and so did I.\", \"mainImage\": {\"_updatedAt\": \"2019-09-24T19:14:52.386000\", \"contentTypeId\": \"image\", \"contentfulId\": \"5ovqJqOrkt8SMBucS1YTD9\", \"entryTitle\": \"HP-F1-article-portrait-sorted-into-slytherin-4913\", \"image\": {\"_updatedAt\": \"2019-09-24T19:14:34.008000\", \"contentTypeId\": \"asset\", \"contentfulId\": \"5s6pi6gUfwUkGy7iDCGCzu\", \"file\": [{\"_updatedAt\": \"2019-10-04T14:39:07.875000\", \"contentTypeId\": \"textSection\", \"contentfulId\": \"3WuxVkKSqhwRT0l8D5VQKU\", \"entryTitle\": \"2019-09-25-ISSUE8-ARTICLE-OPED-TEXTSECTION-tait-amelia-learned-stop-worrying-love-being-Slytherin\", \"text\": \"It was 2013 and I just had completed Pottermore\\u2019s Sorting Experience. \\u2018Congratulations on being sorted into Slytherin,\\u2019 the page read \\u2013 but I didn\\u2019t feel there was anything worth celebrating. I had very recently hurt somebody close to me, so in my eyes, the Sorting Hat might as well have said: \\u2018You\\u2019re a bad person, and everything you feared about yourself is true.\\u2019 Embarrassing as it is to admit now, I cried. \\n\\nWhy did I have such a strong reaction to being sorted with the serpents? Merlin aside, and before the events of *Cursed Child*, Slytherin alumni don\\u2019t have the best of reputations. \\u2018There\\u2019s not a single witch or wizard who went bad who wasn\\u2019t in Slytherin,\\u2019 Hagrid famously said \\u2013 but just because nearly all bad wizards are Slytherins doesn\\u2019t mean all Slytherins are bad wizards. Severus Snape, Horace Slughorn, and Regulus Black were all Slytherin heroes in their own way, and the \\u2018evil house\\u2019 is full of great traits such as resourcefulness, determination, cleverness, and \\u2013 in the words of Albus Dumbledore \\u2013 \\u2018a certain disregard for the rules\\u2019.  \\n\\nMaud is a 17-year-old Potter fan who felt \\u2018insecure\\u2019 when she was sorted into Slytherin six years ago, at the same age Harry was when he muttered \\u2018not Slytherin\\u2019 in front of the Great Hall. \\u2018I thought I would be a Ravenclaw,\\u201d Maud says now, \\u2018When I first found out I was a Slytherin, it was a mixture of feeling insecure \\u2013 comparing myself to the most famous Slytherins and asking myself if I was a bully like them \\u2013 and pride in being an ambitious, hard-working person.\\u2019 Nearly all of the bullies in the books are Slytherins, and the house has a negative reputation for valuing self-preservation above all else. \\u2018They were always made out to be monsters, so being grouped with that was a little saddening,\\u2019 says Maud. She and I are not the only people who felt sad after being sorted.\\n\\n\\u2018When my Slytherin result popped up, my stomach sank,\\u2019 says 39-year-old Sharann, who had also assumed she was a Ravenclaw. \\u2018I felt like deleting my account and starting over. I am not a particularly ambitious person in the traditional sense, I was raised in poverty, and since Draco is really the main Slytherin we see throughout the books, I just felt out of place.\\u2019 Draco Malfoy also meant that 19-year-old Stephanie Adams was \\u2018confused and upset\\u2019 by her result. \\u201cHe was one of my least favourite characters,\\u201d she says, \\u2018and I didn\\u2019t want to be sorted in the same house he was in, as I saw it as a kind of \\u201cbad\\u201d house.\\u2019\\n\\nUnsurprisingly, the Harry Potter books are very much told from Harry Potter\\u2019s perspective, so it makes sense that the Boy Who Lived doesn\\u2019t see many redeeming qualities in the house of his enemies. Outside of the books, J.K. Rowling has given a fuller picture of Slytherins and their traits. In an interview with *Leaky Cauldron* in 2007, Rowling clarified that some Slytherins were among the reinforcements Horace Slughorn bought to the Battle of Hogwarts. \\u2018They\\u2019re not all bad,\\u2019 she said at the time, \\u2018A part of the final battle that made me smile was Slughorn galloping back with the Slytherins.\\u2019 \\n\\n\\u2018They\\u2019d gone off to get reinforcements first \\u2026 But yes, they came back, they came back to fight. I\\u2019m sure that many people would say \\u201cWell, that\\u2019s common sense, isn\\u2019t it? Isn\\u2019t that smart, to get out, get more people and come back with them?\\u201d\\u2019\\n\\nSlytherins are brave, then, they are just more calculated (and some might say cleverer) than wand-happy Gryffindors. Reading more about Slytherin helped Sharann come to terms with her house. \\u2018I even looked up the Sorting Hat songs,\\u2019 she says. \\u2018Cunning isn\\u2019t so bad, I\\u2019m crafty and I think humour does fall into that type of person.\\u2019 \\u2018And while I\\u2019m not ambitious to get that fancy car or big house, I\\u2019m ambitious in having fun, and helping people have a good time and be cheery. I just needed to realise that ambition isn\\u2019t always about material goods.\\u2019\\n\\nJoff is a 40-year-old who was sorted into Slytherin three years ago and was initially \\u2018surprised and a little disappointed\\u2019. However, he now says he is \\u2018proud\\u2019 of his house. \\u2018I changed my mind when I saw the welcome letter (on Pottermore),\\u2019 he says. \\u2018I\\u2019ve seen it said that Slytherins are achievement-oriented and that resonates with me. I always push myself to succeed in anything I do.\\u2019 Stephanie came to terms with being a Slytherin when she realised that the house she initially wanted to be in \\u2013 brave and true Gryffindor \\u2013 wasn\\u2019t all it was cracked up to be.  \\n\\n'Being brave can sometimes mean that you are, in a way, stupid,\\u2019 she says. \\u2018A Gryffindor would die for their friend, while a Slytherin would find a way for both of them to survive. I think that is a smarter way to protect your friends, because you can protect them over and over\\u2026 I\\u2019m proud to be a Slytherin now!\\u2019 Maud says being a Slytherin makes her \\u201cfeel like a leader\\u201d.  \\n\\nIn *Harry Potter and the Philosopher\\u2019s Stone*, Ron Weasley declared that he would\\u2019ve \\u2018got the train straight back home\\u2019 if he was sorted into Slytherin. But it is words from the last book, not the first, that we must remember. A sentiment that was explored in *Harry Potter and the Cursed Child*. \\u2018Albus Severus,\\u2019 a grown Harry told his son quietly, so that nobody but Ginny could hear, \\u2018you were named for two headmasters of Hogwarts. One of them was a Slytherin and he was probably the bravest man I ever knew.\\u2019  \"}], \"tags\": [{\"_updatedAt\": \"2019-08-01T11:51:53.952000\", \"contentTypeId\": \"tag\", \"contentfulId\": \"3B1lhNkNAFaVH3lS0WLMxV\", \"name\": \"feature\"}, {\"_updatedAt\": \"2019-09-20T03:41:18.386000\", \"contentTypeId\": \"tag\", \"contentfulId\": \"L1Cef6BUiA2eC84VPklgq\", \"name\": \"hide-from-app\"}, {\"_updatedAt\": \"2019-07-22T14:27:52.291000\", \"authorComment\": \"This excludes the content item from its index page i.e. quizzes run to Quiz section automatically, but for other Quiz content (publishing elsewhere) it excludes from Discover. And we were there to see it all kick off!\", \"mainImage\": {\"_updatedAt\": \"2019-10-24T16:57:11.233000\", \"contentTypeId\": \"image\", \"contentfulId\": \"51iNo2d2Jb6792yDa67OoM\", \"entryTitle\": \"NEWS-public-previews-begin-in-san-francisco-for-harry-potter-and-the-cursed-child-HERO-IMAGE\", \"image\": {\"_updatedAt\": \"2019-10-24T16:57:00.836000\", \"contentTypeId\": \"asset\", \"contentfulId\": \"69Qa9hDpHZFnXUoZhNGRYv\", \"description\": \"Credit: Drew Altizer Photography\", \"file\": {\"contentType\": \"image/jpeg\", \"details\": {\"image\": {\"height\": 2173, \"width\": 3260}, \"size\": 932531}, \"fileName\": \"0518-HPCC-191023.jpg\", \"url\": \"//images.ctfassets.net/usf1vwtuqyxm/69Qa9hDpHZFnXUoZhNGRYv/4157e2c5e4dad435afa0aaab40dc8a84/0518-HPCC-191023.jpg\"}, \"title\": \"NEWS-public-previews-begin-in-san-francisco-for-harry-potter-and-the-cursed-child-HERO-IMAGE\"}, \"imageAltText\": \"Credit: Drew Altizer Photography\", \"imageCaption\": \"Credit: Drew Altizer Photography\", \"rightsStatement\": \"Credit: Drew Altizer Photography\"}, \"publishDate\": \"2019-10-23T23:00:00\", \"section\": [{\"_updatedAt\": \"2019-10-24T23:13:11.942000\", \"contentTypeId\": \"textSection\", \"contentfulId\": \"5pboZyKj9nRGXecHM2eRNm\", \"entryTitle\": \"public-previews-begin-in-san-francisco-for-harry-potter-and-the-cursed-child-text-section-1\", \"text\": \"San Francisco Potter fans, this is your time. Today, the first preview performances of *Cursed Child* at the Curran Theatre kicked off \\u2013 and we were there to say hello to the cast and fans. \\n\\nSo, while the show doesn\\u2019t officially open until December, the preview performances are now underway. As such, you can bet there are wizarding celebrations aplenty. To start off, San Francisco\\u2019s City Hall got in on the action, bathed in the coloured lights representing the four Hogwarts houses. A strong look, we\\u2019re sure you\\u2019ll all agree.\\n\"}, {\"_updatedAt\": \"2019-10-24T16:57:11.233000\", \"contentTypeId\": \"image\", \"contentfulId\": \"51iNo2d2Jb6792yDa67OoM\", \"entryTitle\": \"NEWS-public-previews-begin-in-san-francisco-for-harry-potter-and-the-cursed-child-HERO-IMAGE\", \"image\": {\"_updatedAt\": \"2019-10-24T16:57:00.836000\", \"contentTypeId\": \"asset\", \"contentfulId\": \"69Qa9hDpHZFnXUoZhNGRYv\", \"description\": \"Credit: Drew Altizer Photography\", \"file\": {\"contentType\": \"image/jpeg\", \"details\": {\"image\": {\"height\": 2173, \"width\": 3260}, \"size\": 932531}, \"fileName\": \"0518-HPCC-191023.jpg\", \"url\": \"//images.ctfassets.net/usf1vwtuqyxm/69Qa9hDpHZFnXUoZhNGRYv/4157e2c5e4dad435afa0aaab40dc8a84/0518-HPCC-191023.jpg\"}, \"title\": \"NEWS-public-previews-begin-in-san-francisco-for-harry-potter-and-the-cursed-child-HERO-IMAGE\"}, \"imageAltText\": \"Credit: Drew Altizer Photography\", \"imageCaption\": \"Credit: Drew Altizer Photography\", \"rightsStatement\": \"Credit: Drew Altizer Photography\"}, {\"_updatedAt\": \"2019-10-25T09:18:39.868000\", \"contentTypeId\": \"textSection\", \"contentfulId\": \"5p3eeodMSmioF84heEGWCr\", \"entryTitle\": \"public-previews-begin-in-san-francisco-for-harry-potter-and-the-cursed-child-text-section-2\", \"text\": \"Earlier this month, we told you about some special [Hogwarts house homecoming parties](https://www.wizardingworld.com/news/hogwarts-house-homecoming-for-cursed-child-in-san-francisco) that were taking place to celebrate the festivities in style, with lucky lottery winners in attendance. Well, those winners got to experience their prize this week, and were treated to some lavish wizarding parties, complete with d\\u00e9cor, food, drink, games, and some very impressive costumes before seeing the show.\\n\\n\"}, {\"_updatedAt\": \"2019-10-25T09:26:36.587000\", \"contentTypeId\": \"textSection\", \"contentfulId\": \"2JOb9g8ZXEjzIASPDzLwZ6\", \"entryTitle\": \"public-previews-begin-in-san-francisco-for-harry-potter-and-the-cursed-child-text-section-3\", \"text\": \"Seeing as *Cursed Child* opens with a young Albus Potter deliberating which Hogwarts house he\\u2019ll be in, we thought we\\u2019d ask fans what they loved the most about their own Hogwarts house. (Remember, you can always discover you house with the reimagined Sorting Ceremony right [here](https://my.wizardingworld.com/sorting-hat)!) Here\\u2019s what they said... \\n\"}, {\"_updatedAt\": \"2019-10-25T09:37:34.766000\", \"contentTypeId\": \"textSection\", \"contentfulId\": \"70FDuu0i2VcmGYqrxoFPpf\", \"entryTitle\": \"public-previews-begin-in-san-francisco-for-harry-potter-and-the-cursed-child-text-section-5\", \"text\": \"Speaking of the cast, ([of which you can learn all about here](https://www.harrypottertheplay.com/san-francisco/cast-creative/)) we sat down with some of them to talk about the upcoming show, what Harry Potter means to them, and how they\\u2019re feeling being part of the ever-extending Wizarding World family. \"}, {\"_updatedAt\": \"2019-10-25T09:33:43.701000\", \"contentTypeId\": \"textSection\", \"contentfulId\": \"3XRMvrBNiz6wkp8T10f3Yt\", \"entryTitle\": \"public-previews-begin-in-san-francisco-for-harry-potter-and-the-cursed-child-text-section-6\", \"text\": \"In fact, many of the cast have Potter connections already. John Skelley understudied Jamie Parker in New York, David Abeles, playing Ron, and Angela Reed, playing Ginny, both previously appeared in the New York company too, while Jon Steiger, AKA Scorpius Malfoy, worked at the Lyric Theatre (where *Cursed Child*\\u2019s New York production takes place) as an usher! It\\u2019s a small Wizarding World, after all.\"}, {\"_updatedAt\": \"2019-10-24T16:24:37.596000\", \"contentTypeId\": \"textSection\", \"contentfulId\": \"7cly8wu3mejdKXpeNHNbps\", \"entryTitle\": \"public-previews-begin-in-san-francisco-for-harry-potter-and-the-cursed-child-text-section-8\", \"text\": \"So, now the curtains have finally gone up on *Cursed Child* in San Francisco, we expect we\\u2019ll be seeing a lot more from this lot as the production starts its journey from previews to opening night. Rowling\\u2019s children\\u2019s charity, is launching an incredible new sweepstake that promises Harry Potter fans the trip of a lifetime.\", \"mainImage\": {\"_updatedAt\": \"2019-10-03T16:18:46.105000\", \"contentTypeId\": \"image\", \"contentfulId\": \"1Hv6CxNc7QHbp9gDww6nHa\", \"entryTitle\": \"lumos-trip-of-a-lifetime-2019-cursed-child-trunks\", \"image\": {\"_updatedAt\": \"2019-10-03T16:18:40.969000\", \"contentTypeId\": \"asset\", \"contentfulId\": \"SoVXqnLv0GqSq7VHklCSK\", \"file\": {\"contentType\": \"image/jpeg\", \"details\": {\"image\": {\"height\": 828, \"width\": 960}, \"size\": 943866}, \"fileName\": \"Lumos_Banner_960x828_1[12].jpg\", \"url\": \"//images.ctfassets.net/usf1vwtuqyxm/SoVXqnLv0GqSq7VHklCSK/beb8baef505516bfacfb61931a27cd0f/Lumos_Banner_960x828_1_12_.jpg\"}, \"title\": \"lumos-trip-of-a-lifetime-2019-cursed-child-trunks\"}}, \"publishDate\": \"2019-10-03T16:00:00\", \"section\": [{\"_updatedAt\": \"2019-10-03T16:22:02.475000\", \"contentTypeId\": \"textSection\", \"contentfulId\": \"6V2nBGtrtXV3YBwp5NYvr9\", \"entryTitle\": \"experience-a-harry-potter-trip-of-a-lifetime-text-section\", \"text\": \"Hold on to your broomsticks, because Lumos is making it possible for one winner and three friends to embark on the ultimate journey to experience the magic of the Wizarding World. It features a host of galleons-can\\u2019t-buy experiences in San Francisco, Los Angeles, Orlando and London.\\n\\nOn the trip, the magical experiences will include: tickets to the opening night of *Harry Potter and the Cursed Child* in San Francisco; a visit to the Warner Bros. Studio Tour London \\u2013 the Making of Harry Potter; and entry to The Wizarding World of Harry Potter at Universal Orlando Resort and Universal Studios Hollywood. All the experiences promise VIP access, amazing seats (in the case of *Cursed Child*) and 4-star accommodation. Well you wouldn\\u2019t expect to be put up at the Leaky Cauldron, would you?  \\n\\nNot only that, the winner (yes, just the winner we\\u2019re afraid) will receive a personalized Hogwarts trunk and a copy of the *Harry Potter and the Cursed Child* playscript signed by J.K. Rowling, John Tiffany and Jack Thorne.\\n\\nThe winner and friends will also have the chance to meet Harry Potter film stars Bonnie Wright in Los Angeles and Warwick Davis in London.\\n\\nBonnie, a Lumos ambassador, says: \\u2018This really will be a once in a lifetime trip for one lucky Harry Potter fan, and the best part is that all donations will support Lumos do their fantastic work to help children around the world to find a family. I can\\u2019t wait to meet the lucky winner when they come to LA - so get entering today, and it could be you.\\u2019\\n\\nThe sweepstake runs from 3 October \\u2013 12 November 2019 and is open to UK and US residents only. Find out how to enter [here](https://www.wearelumos.org/get-involved/trip-of-a-lifetime/). Good luck!\\n\"}], \"shortDescription\": \" Experience a Harry Potter trip of a lifetime\", \"tags\": [{\"_updatedAt\": \"2019-07-22T14:26:23.778000\", \"authorComment\": \"Pins content to top of News or Features index, and removes from list below\", \"contentTypeId\": \"tag\", \"contentfulId\": \"E5YPjsuqMhJPketQjOM1H\", \"name\": \"promoted\"}], \"yoursMagically\": false}], \"primaryCarousel\": [{\"_updatedAt\": \"2019-10-25T13:31:15.529000\", \"activationDate\": \"2019-10-24T23:00:00\", \"author\": {\"_updatedAt\": \"2019-08-01T13:33:18.816000\", \"contentTypeId\": \"author\", \"contentfulId\": \"3moP55ZKIanB6wWwRtA4Ea\", \"displayTitle\": \"Written by\", \"entryTitle\": \"Signature-WizardingWorld\", \"mainImage\": {\"_updatedAt\": \"2019-08-01T11:07:44.068000\", \"contentTypeId\": \"asset\", \"contentfulId\": \"30OscCI83JoLGsI4MKRnJS\", \"file\": {\"contentType\": \"image/jpeg\", \"details\": {\"image\": {\"height\": 360, \"width\": 360}, \"size\": 36037}, \"fileName\": \"WizardingWorldLogo.jpg\", \"url\": \"//images.ctfassets.net/usf1vwtuqyxm/30OscCI83JoLGsI4MKRnJS/2ebebe784733ba3b6a185a8e404e57f7/WizardingWorldLogo.jpg\"}, \"title\": \"Signature_Logo_WizardingWorld\"}, \"title\": \"The Wizarding World Team\"}, \"contentTypeId\": \"article\", \"contentfulId\": \"7wM6u8BwbJSQHyH5qSvAd1\", \"displayTag\": [{\"_updatedAt\": \"2019-07-22T14:25:53.282000\", \"contentTypeId\": \"tag\", \"contentfulId\": \"6PK6KxaPndhQsAFS54UCkr\", \"name\": \"news\"}], \"displayTitle\": \"The story behind the cover of Keys and Curios\", \"entryTitle\": \"NEWS-WEB-the-story-behind-the-cover-of-keys-and-curios\", \"externalId\": \"the-story-behind-the-cover-of-keys-and-curios\", \"intro\": \"The new personalised journal, Keys and Curios, which you can now get hold of if you pre-order Wizarding World Gold, is bound with a very special cover helmed by the graphic design team, MinaLima. Read on to learn more about Gold, and the story behind Keys and Curios\\u2019 cover.\", \"mainImage\": {\"_updatedAt\": \"2019-10-25T13:38:17.660000\", \"contentTypeId\": \"image\", \"contentfulId\": \"BI5B809ZkKYbY6zqeafjC\", \"entryTitle\": \"NEWS-WEB-the-story-behind-the-cover-of-keys-and-curios-HERO-IMAGE\", \"image\": {\"_updatedAt\": \"2019-10-25T13:38:13.507000\", \"contentTypeId\": \"asset\", \"contentfulId\": \"pFbJQtxoef8okKJLD3rtp\", \"file\": {\"contentType\": \"image/jpeg\", \"details\": {\"image\": {\"height\": 1121, \"width\": 2000}, \"size\": 591821}, \"fileName\": \"WW_Journal_range_on paper_rt.jpg\", \"url\": \"//images.ctfassets.net/usf1vwtuqyxm/pFbJQtxoef8okKJLD3rtp/43997bf99ac52c0aa301251a7bcf3121/WW_Journal_range_on_paper_rt.jpg\"}, \"title\": \"NEWS-WEB-the-story-behind-the-cover-of-keys-and-curios-HERO-IMAGE-2\"}}, \"publishDate\": \"2019-10-24T23:00:00\", \"section\": [{\"_updatedAt\": \"2019-10-25T13:41:08.896000\", \"contentTypeId\": \"textSection\", \"contentfulId\": \"3wVUqtOzdDJYCoYomUrMlj\", \"entryTitle\": \"NEWS-WEB-the-story-behind-the-cover-of-keys-and-curios\", \"text\": \"*Keys and Curios* is the title of our new [Wizarding World Gold](https://www.wizardingworld.com/about-gold) journal, a personalised experience lovingly bound together with special covers from MinaLima. The graphic design team, headed by Miraphora Mina and Eduardo Lima, worked on making the journals extra special with these Hogwarts-house themed looks. You can take a look at them right here.\\n\\n\u003cstyle\u003e.embed-container { position: relative; padding-bottom: 56.25%; height: 0; overflow: hidden; max-width: 100%; } .embed-container iframe, .embed-container object, .embed-container embed { position: absolute; top: 0; left: 0; width: 100%; height: 100%; }\u003c/style\u003e\u003cdiv class='embed-container'\u003e\u003ciframe width=\\\"560\\\" height=\\\"315\\\" src=\\\"https://www.youtube.com/embed/XUmrbumv5nk\\\" frameborder=\\\"0\\\" allow=\\\"accelerometer; autoplay; encrypted-media; gyroscope; picture-in-picture\\\" allowfullscreen\u003e\u003c/iframe\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\\n\\nAs you can see, this special journal, [which comes to those who pre-order Wizarding World Gold](https://www.wizardingworld.com/about-gold), is filled with little surprises both inside and out. It\\u2019s also designed to co-ordinate with our Wizarding World app, where you\\u2019ll be able to scan the pages for some extra magical goodness.\\n\\nTo celebrate the *Keys and Curios* unveiling, we spoke to the MinaLima team to discuss the joys of designing book covers. After all, watch any Harry Potter or Fantastic Beasts film, and you\\u2019re guaranteed to spot some of MinaLima\\u2019s previous work in a scene, be it a book cover, a poster or a front page of a wizarding newspaper. So how was it working on this unique project? \\n\\n\\u2018Whenever we\\u2019re invited to do anything for the Wizarding World, it always feels like we\\u2019ve come home,\\u2019 MinaLima told us. \\n\\n\\u2018And the work we did for the fiction, which could be absolutely anything, informed some of the decisions when it comes to designing things for the real world. I guess one similar moment that springs to mind is designing the screenplay to *Fantastic Beasts*, which was almost coming full circle.\\u2019 \\n\\nWhen it came to the team crafting the front of *Keys and Curios*, you\\u2019ll notice from the covers that there\\u2019s an astronomical theme to them, along with some graphic elements that depict the passing of time. For example, eagle-eyed fans may spot a nod to the Time-Turner, which is subtly woven into the structure of the cover\\u2019s designs. \\n\\n\\u2018There\\u2019s this theme of time,\\u2019 Mira noted. \\u2018[The journal] is capturing a year of your personal life. And it might be something you look on later. So, I think the element of time was important, rather than just being \\u201ca book\\u201d. So the little cheeky nod to putting in the text from the Time-Turner will hopefully resonate with people.\\u2019\\n\\nThe books also have a distinct space-y look to them, as well as little details associated with each Hogwarts house.\\n\\n\\u2018With some of the visual references, like the house crests, we\\u2019ve given them a slight constellation element, as if it\\u2019s something a little bit beyond the world we\\u2019re inhabiting now,\\u2019 the team explained. We\\u2019re sure Professor Trelawney would approve.\\n\\nSo, there you have it. If you\\u2019d like to read more about Wizarding World Gold, and pick up your very own personalised version of *Keys and Curios*, learn all about it right [here](https://www.wizardingworld.com/about-gold). \\n\\nAnd MinaLima fans will also be excited to learn that the Gold membership comes with another little treat coming soon: a 10% online discount to use at MinaLima\\u2019s [shop](https://minalima.com/shop-minalima/) (excluding premium prints and other non-mass produced products).\\n\\nAgain, pop by our about page [to find out more](https://www.wizardingworld.com/about-gold), and watch this space to learn about future developments with Wizarding World Gold.\"}], \"tags\": [{\"_updatedAt\": \"2019-07-22T14:27:52.291000\", \"authorComment\": \"This excludes the content item from its index page i.e. quizzes run to Quiz section automatically, but for other Quiz content (publishing elsewhere) it excludes from Discover. And we were there to see it all kick off!\", \"mainImage\": {\"_updatedAt\": \"2019-10-24T16:57:11.233000\", \"contentTypeId\": \"image\", \"contentfulId\": \"51iNo2d2Jb6792yDa67OoM\", \"entryTitle\": \"NEWS-public-previews-begin-in-san-francisco-for-harry-potter-and-the-cursed-child-HERO-IMAGE\", \"image\": {\"_updatedAt\": \"2019-10-24T16:57:00.836000\", \"contentTypeId\": \"asset\", \"contentfulId\": \"69Qa9hDpHZFnXUoZhNGRYv\", \"description\": \"Credit: Drew Altizer Photography\", \"file\": {\"contentType\": \"image/jpeg\", \"details\": {\"image\": {\"height\": 2173, \"width\": 3260}, \"size\": 932531}, \"fileName\": \"0518-HPCC-191023.jpg\", \"url\": \"//images.ctfassets.net/usf1vwtuqyxm/69Qa9hDpHZFnXUoZhNGRYv/4157e2c5e4dad435afa0aaab40dc8a84/0518-HPCC-191023.jpg\"}, \"title\": \"NEWS-public-previews-begin-in-san-francisco-for-harry-potter-and-the-cursed-child-HERO-IMAGE\"}, \"imageAltText\": \"Credit: Drew Altizer Photography\", \"imageCaption\": \"Credit: Drew Altizer Photography\", \"rightsStatement\": \"Credit: Drew Altizer Photography\"}, \"publishDate\": \"2019-10-23T23:00:00\", \"section\": [{\"_updatedAt\": \"2019-10-24T23:13:11.942000\", \"contentTypeId\": \"textSection\", \"contentfulId\": \"5pboZyKj9nRGXecHM2eRNm\", \"entryTitle\": \"public-previews-begin-in-san-francisco-for-harry-potter-and-the-cursed-child-text-section-1\", \"text\": \"San Francisco Potter fans, this is your time. Today, the first preview performances of *Cursed Child* at the Curran Theatre kicked off \\u2013 and we were there to say hello to the cast and fans. \\n\\nSo, while the show doesn\\u2019t officially open until December, the preview performances are now underway. As such, you can bet there are wizarding celebrations aplenty. To start off, San Francisco\\u2019s City Hall got in on the action, bathed in the coloured lights representing the four Hogwarts houses. A strong look, we\\u2019re sure you\\u2019ll all agree.\\n\"}, {\"_updatedAt\": \"2019-10-24T16:57:11.233000\", \"contentTypeId\": \"image\", \"contentfulId\": \"51iNo2d2Jb6792yDa67OoM\", \"entryTitle\": \"NEWS-public-previews-begin-in-san-francisco-for-harry-potter-and-the-cursed-child-HERO-IMAGE\", \"image\": {\"_updatedAt\": \"2019-10-24T16:57:00.836000\", \"contentTypeId\": \"asset\", \"contentfulId\": \"69Qa9hDpHZFnXUoZhNGRYv\", \"description\": \"Credit: Drew Altizer Photography\", \"file\": {\"contentType\": \"image/jpeg\", \"details\": {\"image\": {\"height\": 2173, \"width\": 3260}, \"size\": 932531}, \"fileName\": \"0518-HPCC-191023.jpg\", \"url\": \"//images.ctfassets.net/usf1vwtuqyxm/69Qa9hDpHZFnXUoZhNGRYv/4157e2c5e4dad435afa0aaab40dc8a84/0518-HPCC-191023.jpg\"}, \"title\": \"NEWS-public-previews-begin-in-san-francisco-for-harry-potter-and-the-cursed-child-HERO-IMAGE\"}, \"imageAltText\": \"Credit: Drew Altizer Photography\", \"imageCaption\": \"Credit: Drew Altizer Photography\", \"rightsStatement\": \"Credit: Drew Altizer Photography\"}, {\"_updatedAt\": \"2019-10-25T09:18:39.868000\", \"contentTypeId\": \"textSection\", \"contentfulId\": \"5p3eeodMSmioF84heEGWCr\", \"entryTitle\": \"public-previews-begin-in-san-francisco-for-harry-potter-and-the-cursed-child-text-section-2\", \"text\": \"Earlier this month, we told you about some special [Hogwarts house homecoming parties](https://www.wizardingworld.com/news/hogwarts-house-homecoming-for-cursed-child-in-san-francisco) that were taking place to celebrate the festivities in style, with lucky lottery winners in attendance. Well, those winners got to experience their prize this week, and were treated to some lavish wizarding parties, complete with d\\u00e9cor, food, drink, games, and some very impressive costumes before seeing the show.\\n\\n\"}, {\"_updatedAt\": \"2019-10-25T09:26:36.587000\", \"contentTypeId\": \"textSection\", \"contentfulId\": \"2JOb9g8ZXEjzIASPDzLwZ6\", \"entryTitle\": \"public-previews-begin-in-san-francisco-for-harry-potter-and-the-cursed-child-text-section-3\", \"text\": \"Seeing as *Cursed Child* opens with a young Albus Potter deliberating which Hogwarts house he\\u2019ll be in, we thought we\\u2019d ask fans what they loved the most about their own Hogwarts house. (Remember, you can always discover you house with the reimagined Sorting Ceremony right [here](https://my.wizardingworld.com/sorting-hat)!) Here\\u2019s what they said... \\n\"}, {\"_updatedAt\": \"2019-10-25T09:37:34.766000\", \"contentTypeId\": \"textSection\", \"contentfulId\": \"70FDuu0i2VcmGYqrxoFPpf\", \"entryTitle\": \"public-previews-begin-in-san-francisco-for-harry-potter-and-the-cursed-child-text-section-5\", \"text\": \"Speaking of the cast, ([of which you can learn all about here](https://www.harrypottertheplay.com/san-francisco/cast-creative/)) we sat down with some of them to talk about the upcoming show, what Harry Potter means to them, and how they\\u2019re feeling being part of the ever-extending Wizarding World family. \"}, {\"_updatedAt\": \"2019-10-25T09:33:43.701000\", \"contentTypeId\": \"textSection\", \"contentfulId\": \"3XRMvrBNiz6wkp8T10f3Yt\", \"entryTitle\": \"public-previews-begin-in-san-francisco-for-harry-potter-and-the-cursed-child-text-section-6\", \"text\": \"In fact, many of the cast have Potter connections already. John Skelley understudied Jamie Parker in New York, David Abeles, playing Ron, and Angela Reed, playing Ginny, both previously appeared in the New York company too, while Jon Steiger, AKA Scorpius Malfoy, worked at the Lyric Theatre (where *Cursed Child*\\u2019s New York production takes place) as an usher! It\\u2019s a small Wizarding World, after all.\"}, {\"_updatedAt\": \"2019-10-24T16:24:37.596000\", \"contentTypeId\": \"textSection\", \"contentfulId\": \"7cly8wu3mejdKXpeNHNbps\", \"entryTitle\": \"public-previews-begin-in-san-francisco-for-harry-potter-and-the-cursed-child-text-section-8\", \"text\": \"So, now the curtains have finally gone up on *Cursed Child* in San Francisco, we expect we\\u2019ll be seeing a lot more from this lot as the production starts its journey from previews to opening night. Watch this space as the *Cursed Child* San Francisco story begins! \"}], \"tags\": [{\"_updatedAt\": \"2019-07-22T14:25:53.282000\", \"contentTypeId\": \"tag\", \"contentfulId\": \"6PK6KxaPndhQsAFS54UCkr\", \"name\": \"news\"}, {\"_updatedAt\": \"2019-07-22T14:27:52.291000\", \"authorComment\": \"This excludes the content item from its index page i.e. quizzes run to Quiz section automatically, but for other Quiz content (publishing elsewhere) it excludes from Discover. \"title\": \"web-10-10-pre-order-gold-hero-image\"}}, \"publishDate\": \"2019-10-14T16:00:00\", \"section\": [{\"_updatedAt\": \"2019-10-16T13:25:55.802000\", \"contentTypeId\": \"textSection\", \"contentfulId\": \"4TrsDVjqz4QmzRLWrd0BEp\", \"entryTitle\": \"NEWS-WEB-TEXTSECTION-introducing-wizarding-world-gold\", \"text\": \"From eBooks to exclusive series, priority ticketing to collectible pins \\u2013 here\\u2019s a guide to the glittering goodies that come with your subscription.\\n\\nAre there any Nifflers around? Keep your eyes peeled for them, because we\\u2019re about to talk about Gold. Launching this autumn, [Wizarding World Gold](http://wizarding.world/AboutGold) is an annual paid subscription that promises to serve up all manner of Wizarding World treats. Currently on offer to UK and US-based fans (with more countries to follow in the coming months), it\\u2019s available to pre-order now and will enhance your free membership of the Official Harry Potter Fan Club.\\n\\nHere are just some of the things on offer\\u2026\\n\\n### A magical welcome gift\\n\\nSubscribers will receive a magical welcome gift, including a postcard-sized print of J.K. Rowling\\u2019s sketch of Hogwarts, an exclusive collectible pin and a personalised, interactive journal we\\u2019re calling *Keys and Curios*. \\n\\n### Curious about *Keys and Curios*? Read on\\u2026\\n\\nThis beautiful journal will arrive personalised with your name, Hogwarts house and more. And *Keys and Curios* knows more about you than just your house \\u2013 flip through its pages to find personalised surprises and, as the title may suggest, discover Enchanted Keys that you can scan with your Wizarding World app to unlock hidden secrets. Each month will offer up something new, display gorgeous themed artwork from across the Wizarding World and propose regular activities for you to scribble in.\\n\\n(And it absolutely won\\u2019t be mistaken for Tom Riddle\\u2019s diary!)\\n\\nDid we mention? The *Keys and Curios* cover is specially designed by the graphic design team behind the *Harry Potter* and *Fantastic Beasts* films, MinaLima.\\n\\nThose that take advantage of the pre-order window can be among the first to receive this amazing journal. We really hope you like it.\\n\\n### And even more magic\\n\\nAs well as your welcome gift, a 12-month Wizarding World Gold subscription will also give you*:\\n\\n\\u2022\\t__Wizarding World Originals__ \\u2013 Our new exclusive video series, set to unravel the mysteries and uncover the secrets from all corners of the Wizarding World.\\n\\n\\u2022\\t__All 7 eBooks of the original Harry Potter stories__ \\u2013 Take the magic of J.K. Rowling\\u2019s stories wherever you go with these 7 eBooks, available on the Wizarding World app for the duration of your subscription. \\n\\n\\u2022\\t__Collectible pin badges__ \\u2013 You\\u2019ll receive the first pin badge in your welcome gift. But there are more to collect!\\n\\n\\u2022\\t__Special events__ \\u2013 Access Gold subscriber events throughout the year, such as the Wizarding World Gold Christmas Party in the Great Hall at Warner Bros. Studio Tour London - The Making of Harry Potter, later this year.\\n\\n\\u2022\\t__Exclusive discounts__ \\u2013 Enjoy discounts from the Wizarding World.com shop, Platform 9\\u00be store in London\\u2019s King\\u2019s Cross Station, and shops within Warner Bros. Studio Tour London \\u2013 The Making of Harry Potter and Warner Bros. Studio Tour Hollywood, as well as discounts on The Wizarding World of Harry Potter\\u2122 Exclusive Vacation Package at Universal Orlando Resort.\\n\\n\\u2022\\t__Priority booking__ \\u2013 Priority access to tickets for the most popular Wizarding World events and locations, including Harry Potter and the Cursed Child shows in London, New York and San Francisco as well as Warner Bros. Studio Tour London \\u2013 The Making of Harry Potter. \\n\\n\\u2022\\t__Early access__ \\u2013 Unlock early access to limited-edition Wizarding World Gold merchandise ranges and curious collectibles - before they go on general release. \\n\\n\\u2022\\t__Plus, plenty of perks__ \\u2013 including new quizzes and puzzles, chances to win once in-a-lifetime experiences and much, much more! \\n\\n__Enjoy all this for just $74.99 (US) and \\u00a359.99 (UK).__\\n\\n*Certain Gold benefits are subject to availability and change from time to time. Some exclusions and other conditions may apply.\\n\\n*Any extra questions on Wizarding World Gold? [Click here](http://wizarding.world/AboutGold) to learn more. And watch out for peeping Nifflers!*\\n\"}], \"shortDescription\": \"Introducing Wizarding World Gold\", \"tags\": [{\"_updatedAt\": \"2019-09-20T03:41:18.386000\", \"contentTypeId\": \"tag\", \"contentfulId\": \"L1Cef6BUiA2eC84VPklgq\", \"name\": \"hide-from-app\"}, {\"_updatedAt\": \"2019-07-22T14:27:52.291000\", \"authorComment\": \"This excludes the content item from its index page i.e. quizzes run to Quiz section automatically, but for other Quiz content (publishing elsewhere) it excludes from Discover.
